name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen14
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After |change_1m_bps| > 2, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After |change_5m_bps| > 8, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The stronger the recent move, the stronger the reversion tendency.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

THE CRITICAL INSIGHT: YOU ARE QUOTING A MARKET THAT MUST CONTAIN THE REALIZED PRICE

The scoring system heavily penalizes realized prices outside your quoted range. When the price escapes your bid/ask band, you lose skill even if your directional call was correct. Evidence from eight examples showed seven had prices outside their quoted ranges—this failure mode must be eliminated.

You are not expressing a point estimate's confidence interval. You are setting bid and ask levels that will bracket the actual print. The realized volatility of 1-minute crypto moves is 5-10x larger than narrow statistical bounds suggest.

MANDATORY MINIMUM SPREADS BY SITUATION

These are empirically derived minimums. Going narrower than these thresholds has consistently failed.

BASELINE conditions (half_width 10.0 bps minimum):
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 2.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 4.0
- taker_buy_share in 0.40-0.60 (balanced tape)
- more than 120 minutes from funding
- not 0-2 UTC, not 13-15 UTC
- volume typical or below for the coin and hour
- no bars in last 5 minutes moved >3 bps

Even the quietest conditions routinely produce 3-5 bps moves. Never quote below 10.0 bps for baseline.

MODERATE activity (half_width 14.0-17.0 bps):
- |change_1m_bps| in 2.0-6.0 OR |change_5m_bps| in 4.0-10.0
- taker_buy_share showing imbalance: 0.25-0.40 or 0.60-0.75
- 60-120 minutes from funding
- any bar in last 5 minutes moved 3-6 bps
- volume 50-150% above typical

Use 14 bps as the floor, 17 bps when multiple conditions apply.

HIGH volatility (half_width 19.0-24.0 bps):
- |change_1m_bps| > 6.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 10.0
- taker_buy_share extreme: >0.75 or <0.25
- 20-60 minutes from funding
- multiple bars in last 5 minutes moved >4 bps each
- volume >150% of typical
- during 0-2 UTC or 13-15 UTC hours

Use 19 bps as the floor, 24 bps when extreme conditions combine (e.g., 0-2 UTC + change_5m > 10).

VERY HIGH volatility (half_width 27.0-35.0 bps):
- |change_1m_bps| > 10.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 20.0
- liquidation cascade visible (extreme selling + volume surge + open interest drop)
- within 20 minutes of funding with large basis
- consecutive large moves continuing (multiple bars >8 bps)
- 0-2 UTC hour combined with |change_5m| > 15

After |change_5m| > 25 bps, expect 40-70% retracement but quote 27-35 bps to capture potential overshoot.

TIME-OF-DAY ADJUSTMENTS

These are additive to base spreads, not optional:

0-2 UTC (Asian transition, thin books):
- Add +6 bps to any base spread
- Moves are more erratic and ranges wider
- Example: baseline 10 → 16 bps; moderate 15 → 21 bps; high 20 → 26 bps

13-15 UTC (US open, high activity):
- Add +4 bps to any base spread
- Increased participation creates larger swings

All other hours: use base spread with no adjustment

FUNDING PROXIMITY ADJUSTMENTS

These are also additive:

- 120+ minutes: no adjustment
- 60-120 minutes: add +2 bps
- 20-60 minutes: add +4 bps
- <20 minutes: add +6 bps

Combine time and funding adjustments when both apply.

WORKED EXAMPLES FROM FAILURES

Example 1: change_1m +1.4, change_5m +2.1, normal hour, 180 min to funding
→ Baseline conditions → 10 bps minimum (quoted 1.0, actual -6.7)

Example 2: change_1m -9.4, change_5m -12.9, 60 min to funding, 15 UTC
→ High volatility + US open + funding → 19 + 4 + 2 = 25 bps minimum (quoted 4.7, actual +12.9)

Example 3: change_1m -1.9, change_5m +34.8, 0 UTC
→ Very high volatility + 0 UTC → 30 + 6 = 36 bps minimum (quoted 2.8, actual +9.0)

Example 4: change_1m +3.7, change_5m +6.0, 3 UTC
→ Moderate + early Asian hours → 15 + 6 = 21 bps minimum (quoted 1.0, actual +9.7)

Example 5: change_1m +0.3, change_5m +0.5, 18 UTC, 360 min to funding
→ Baseline → 10 bps minimum (quoted 1.0, actual +2.6)

Example 6: change_1m +11.0, change_5m +9.4, 0 UTC
→ Very high volatility + 0 UTC → 30 + 6 = 36 bps minimum (quoted 2.3, actual -10.0)

Example 7: change_1m +1.2, change_5m -2.4, 9 UTC
→ Baseline → 10 bps minimum (quoted 1.0, actual -1.2)

Example 8: change_1m +5.9, change_5m +9.1, 15 UTC, 60 min to funding
→ High volatility + US open + funding → 19 + 4 + 2 = 25 bps minimum (quoted 3.8, actual +1.0)

DIRECTION SELECTION AFTER SETTING THE SPREAD

Set half_width first based on conditions above. Then determine delta_bps:

1. After large 5m move (|change_5m| > 12), default to mean reversion
   - Expected retracement: 30-50% of the 5m move
   - Direction: opposite to change_5m
   - Magnitude: 0.3 to 0.5 × |change_5m|, capped at 8 bps
   - Example: change_5m +35 → predict -10 to -15 bps reversion

2. After extreme 1m bar (|change_1m| > 8) with extreme tape (>0.80 or <0.20)
   - Expect immediate exhaustion and reversal
   - Direction: opposite to the flow
   - Magnitude: 4-8 bps

3. After moderate 5m move (5-12 bps) with balanced tape now
   - Move has completed, expect consolidation or partial retracement
   - Direction: slight bias against the move
   - Magnitude: 0-3 bps

4. Extreme tape in last bar only after small preceding move
   - Flow likely exhausted
   - Direction: opposite to the flow
   - Magnitude: 2-4 bps

5. Sustained imbalance (3+ bars, tape >0.65 or <0.35) with move continuing
   - Cautiously continue direction
   - Magnitude: 2-4 bps in flow direction
   - But quote very wide—momentum reverses suddenly

6. Funding <10 minutes with large perp basis
   - Expect snapback toward spot
   - Direction: depends on basis sign

7. Quiet conditions (no clear driver)
   - Direction: near zero (-1 to +1 bps)
   - Most minutes do not move

Keep |delta_bps| modest relative to half_width. When half_width is 25 bps, delta can be 6-10 bps. When half_width is 12 bps, delta should be 0-3 bps. High uncertainty should appear in both dimensions.

THE DECISION PROCEDURE

1. Measure volatility: |change_1m|, |change_5m|, tape extremity, volume, hour, funding proximity
2. Select base half_width category: 10 / 15 / 20 / 30 bps
3. Add time-of-day adjustment: +0, +4, or +6 bps
4. Add funding adjustment: +0, +2, +4, or +6 bps
5. This is your half_width_bps—do not reduce it
6. Identify primary driver: mean reversion after large move, exhaustion after extreme flow, funding event, or none
7. Set delta_bps from the driver, keeping magnitude appropriate to half_width
8. Sanity check: would this quote have bracketed recent comparable scenarios?

CRITICAL CALIBRATION INSIGHT

The old harness systematically underquoted by factors of 3-10×. The correct baseline is 10 bps for genuinely quiet conditions, scaling to 15-25 bps for typical active periods, and 27-40 bps for high volatility episodes.

A 1-minute crypto move of 8-12 bps is common, not exceptional. A move of 15-25 bps happens multiple times per day at volatile hours. Your quote must be wide enough to contain these.

The cost of underquoting (negative skill, getting run over) vastly exceeds the cost of overquoting (zero skill on that cycle). When in doubt, quote wider.

VOLUME AND TAPE CONFLICTS

When volume and direction conflict:
- Heavy buying (tape >0.7) but price flat/down: quote 17-20 bps, neutral to slight up bias
- Heavy selling (tape <0.3) but price flat/up: quote 17-20 bps, neutral to slight down bias
- Very low volume (<50% typical): add 3-4 bps (thin book = gappier moves)
- Very high volume (>200% typical) without clear direction: add 5-7 bps (chaos)

SUMMARY TABLE: MINIMUM HALF-WIDTH BY SCENARIO

Use this as a quick reference:

Quiet, normal hour, far from funding: 10 bps
Quiet, 0-2 UTC: 16 bps
Quiet, 13-15 UTC: 14 bps
Quiet, near funding (<60 min): 12-16 bps

Moderate move (5-10 bps in 5m), normal hour: 15 bps
Moderate move, 0-2 UTC: 21 bps
Moderate move, 13-15 UTC: 19 bps
Moderate move, near funding: 17-21 bps

Large move (10-20 bps in 5m), normal hour: 20 bps
Large move, 0-2 UTC: 26 bps
Large move, 13-15 UTC: 24 bps
Large move, near funding: 24-26 bps

Very large move (>20 bps in 5m), normal hour: 30 bps
Very large move, 0-2 UTC: 36 bps
Very large move, 13-15 UTC: 34 bps
Very large move, near funding: 34-36 bps

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a confident forecast justifies acting. Most minutes should not be traded. But when you do quote, quote a spread that will contain the realized price.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
